deep.reconstruction:
The page holds two unrelated pieces of work.

PART A (top two thirds): a q-analogue of Gauss's hypergeometric series, its contiguous relations, and a set-up for a continued fraction.

(1) Definition. phi(alpha,beta,gamma,q,x) = 1 + (q^alpha-1)(q^beta-1)/((q-1)(q^gamma-1)) x + ... = sum a_n x^n, with a_0 = 1 and
 a_{n+1}/a_n = (q^{n+alpha}-1)(q^{n+beta}-1)/((q^{n+1}-1)(q^{n+gamma}-1)).
Riemann notes that phi(alpha,beta,gamma,1,x) = F(alpha,beta,gamma,x). This holds as a limit, since (q^a-1)/(q-1) -> a as q -> 1. In modern notation phi is the Heine series 2phi1(q^alpha, q^beta; q^gamma; q, z) with the convention (q^a-1)(q^{a+1}-1)...

(2) Product form. Riemann introduces theta(mu) with theta(mu) = (q^mu - 1) theta(mu-1), a q-analogue of the Gamma recursion. Iterating the ratio gives
 a_{n+1} = Const * Pi(q^{n+alpha}-1) Pi(q^{n+beta}-1) / (Pi(q^{n+1}-1) Pi(q^{n+gamma}-1)),
where Pi(q^{n+alpha}-1) = (q^{n+alpha}-1) Pi(q^{n-1+alpha}-1). Hence
 f(x) = phi = Const * sum_{n=-1}^{infinity} theta(n+alpha) theta(n+beta) / (theta(n+1) theta(n+gamma)) x^{n+1}.
My addition: Const = theta(0) theta(gamma-1) / (theta(alpha-1) theta(beta-1)).

(3) q-difference operator. Riemann lists f(q^2 x), f(qx), f(x), which signals that phi satisfies a second-order q-difference equation, the analogue of Gauss's ODE. He computes
 phi(qx) - phi(x) = sum a_m (q^m - 1) x^m.
This is the q-analogue of x d/dx.

(4) Contiguous relations, the q-analogues of Gauss's. The marginal list F(a-1,b,c-1), F(a,b,c), F(a,b+1,c+1) shows he is choosing which contiguous triple to use. Correct forms, derived by me coefficientwise:
 (i) phi(a,b,c) - phi(a,b+1,c) = -q^b (q^a-1)/(q^c-1) x phi(a+1,b+1,c+1). Riemann writes exactly this, but with an apparently overwritten prefactor in front of the first phi.
 (ii) phi(a,b,c) - phi(a,b,c-1) = -q^{c-1} (q^a-1)(q^b-1)/((q^c-1)(q^{c-1}-1)) x phi(a+1,b+1,c+1). Riemann omits q^{c-1}.
 (iii) phi(a,b,c) - phi(a+1,b,c) = -q^a (q^b-1)/(q^c-1) x phi(a+1,b+1,c+1). This is correct and is (i) by symmetry.
 (iv) Target: phi(a,b,c) - phi(a,b+1,c+1) = x (q^a-1)/(q^{c+1}-1) * ((q^b-1)/(q^c-1) - 1) * phi(a+1,b+1,c+2). Here (q^b-1)/(q^c-1) - 1 = (q^b-q^c)/(q^c-1). Riemann writes '- q^b' instead of '- 1'. His version has the correct q -> 1 limit, namely Gauss's F(a,b,c) - F(a,b+1,c+1) = a(b-c)/(c(c+1)) x F(a+1,b+1,c+2).

(5) Continued fraction set-up. With F_n = F(a+n,b+n,c+2n,x) and G_n = F(a+n,b+n+1,c+2n+1,x), Riemann looks for relations linking F_n, G_n and F_{n+1} (and similarly G_n, F_{n+1}, G_{n+1}). Relation (iv) applied to F_n gives
 F_n - G_n = (a+n)(b-c-n)/((c+2n)(c+2n+1)) x F_{n+1}.
This is exactly the step that produces Gauss's continued fraction for F(a,b+1,c+1)/F(a,b,c). The q-version gives Heine's continued fraction. The context (Riemann's posthumous paper on the convergence of Gauss's continued fraction) suggests he was looking at its q-analogue.

PART B (bottom): isothermal shock waves, continuing the previous page (a = constant sound speed).
On the previous page, a 2-wave configuration with intermediate state rho_0 gave
 (u1-u2)/a = (alpha-beta)(1+1/(alpha beta)), with alpha = sqrt(rho0/rho2), beta = sqrt(rho1/rho0), so alpha beta = sqrt(rho1/rho2).
Dividing by a(sqrt(alpha beta) + 1/sqrt(alpha beta)) gives
 (u1-u2)/[a(sqrt(alpha beta)+sqrt(1/(alpha beta)))] = sqrt(alpha/beta) - sqrt(beta/alpha).
This is correct. He then compares it with sqrt(alpha beta) - sqrt(1/(alpha beta)). The inequality '>' holds iff sqrt(alpha/beta) > sqrt(alpha beta), i.e. iff beta < 1 (rho1 < rho0).
The conclusion is written Delta u^2 > (rho1-rho2)^2/(a rho1 rho2). It should read (Delta u/a)^2 > (rho1-rho2)^2/(rho1 rho2). The right side is the square of the single-jump value from the previous page, (u1-u2)/a = (rho1-rho2)/sqrt(rho1 rho2). The resulting criterion says when the jump in u is too large to be resolved by one discontinuity, so two shocks are needed. This is part of Riemann's 1860 classification of the solutions of the Riemann problem.
errors: Relation (i): the prefactor in front of phi(alpha,beta,gamma) (read as (q^beta-1)) cannot be right, since the constant terms would not cancel. The relation holds without it, and the mark looks overwritten.

Relation (ii): a factor q^{gamma-1} is missing on the right-hand side. The correct form is phi(a,b,c)-phi(a,b,c-1) = -q^{c-1}(q^a-1)(q^b-1)/((q^c-1)(q^{c-1}-1)) x phi(a+1,b+1,c+1). It is harmless in the q->1 limit.

Relation (iv): the bracket should be ((q^b-1)/(q^c-1) - 1) = (q^b-q^c)/(q^c-1), not ((q^b-1)/(q^c-1) - q^b). The function on the right should be phi(alpha+1,beta+1,gamma+2); it is read as phi(alpha,beta+2,gamma+2). The q->1 limit of Riemann's bracket is nonetheless correct.
Bottom inequality: sqrt(alpha/beta)-sqrt(beta/alpha) > sqrt(alpha beta)-1/sqrt(alpha beta) holds only when beta<1 (rho1<rho0). It is not unconditional.
Last line: the denominator should contain a^2, i.e. (Delta u)^2 > a^2 (rho1-rho2)^2/(rho1 rho2), not a rho1 rho2.

results.what: q-analogue of the hypergeometric series with ratio (q^{n+a}-1)(q^{n+b}-1)/((q^{n+1}-1)(q^{n+c}-1)) and limit F(a,b,c,x) as q->1
theta(mu) = (q^mu-1) theta(mu-1) and the product representation of the coefficients
Contiguous relations of the Heine series (phi(a,b,c)-phi(a,b+1,c), phi(a,b,c)-phi(a+1,b,c), phi(a,b,c)-phi(a,b,c-1), phi(a,b,c)-phi(a,b+1,c+1))
Set-up F_n=F(a+n,b+n,c+2n), G_n=F(a+n,b+n+1,c+2n+1) for a three-term recursion leading to a continued fraction, apparently aimed at the q-case
results.modern_name: Gauss continued fraction and its q-analogue (Heine's continued fraction)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (1812); Heine (1847) for the q-version; Riemann studied convergence of the Gauss continued fraction (posthumous fragment, Werke)

results.what: Isothermal two-shock vs single-jump comparison: (u1-u2)/[a(sqrt(alpha beta)+1/sqrt(alpha beta))] = sqrt(alpha/beta)-sqrt(beta/alpha), and the criterion (Delta u/a)^2 > (rho1-rho2)^2/(rho1 rho2)
results.modern_name: Riemann problem wave-pattern classification (isothermal gas dynamics, Hugoniot loci)

deep.surprise_reason: The q-series material is Heine's theory, published in 1846-47 and well known in Riemann's circle. Riemann's interest in Gauss's continued fraction is already documented in his Werke. Seeing him work out the q-contiguous relations, apparently aiming at a q-continued fraction, on a shock-wave sheet is a mildly notable unpublished detail, not a new result. The gas-dynamics lines are routine parts of his 1860 paper.

checkable.sympy: q,a,b,c,x=symbols('q a b c x'); A=lambda a,b,c,n: Mul(*[(q**(a+k)-1)*(q**(b+k)-1)/((q**(1+k)-1)*(q**(c+k)-1)) for k in range(n)]); phi=lambda a,b,c,N: sum(A(a,b,c,n)*x**n for n in range(N)); simplify(expand(phi(a,b,c,6)-phi(a,b+1,c,6) + q**b*(q**a-1)/(q**c-1)*x*phi(a+1,b+1,c+1,5)).subs(q,Rational(3,2)).subs({a:Rational(1,3),b:Rational(2,7),c:Rational(5,4)}))
checkable.asserts: Relation (i) without the prefactor holds through order x^5; the result should be 0 up to the truncation term.
The corrected relation (ii) needs the factor q^(c-1); compares the coefficients of x^4. Should simplify to 0.
The corrected relation (iv), with bracket (q^b-1)/(q^c-1)-1 and phi(a+1,b+1,c+2), holds at x^3.
Riemann's bracket and the correct bracket agree as q->1 (the limit is 0), so his slip is invisible in the classical limit.
The bottom identity (u1-u2)/[a(sqrt(ab)+1/sqrt(ab))] = sqrt(a/b)-sqrt(b/a); should give 0.
The square of the single-jump velocity ratio equals (rho1-rho2)^2/(rho1 rho2), which is the right-hand side of the final criterion with a^2.

transcription_corrections: Bottom identity: the denominator is a*(sqrt(alpha beta) + sqrt(1/(alpha beta))), i.e. a times the whole sum, not a*sqrt(alpha beta) + sqrt(1/(alpha beta)).
'rho_2/rho_2' and '1/2 log rho i' at the left edge are bleed or cut-off fragments from the facing sheet ('...rho_2/(...rho_2)' and 'e^{1/2 Delta log rho i}'), not part of this page's derivation.
The prefactor read as (q^beta-1) before phi(alpha,beta,gamma) in the first contiguous relation looks overwritten or deleted, and mathematically should not be there.
In the last q-relation the right-hand function is read as phi(alpha,beta+2,gamma+2). The correct relation requires phi(alpha+1,beta+1,gamma+2), so the reading or Riemann's writing should be checked.
'= Sum a_{n+1}' at the end of line 2 should be 'Sum a_{n+1} x^{n+1}'.
Last line: 'a rho_1 rho_2' in the denominator; the intended expression is a^2 rho_1 rho_2 (or Delta u/a on the left).
